parts.text: Royal Mail: your parcel is on hold
because of an unpaid shipping fee of £1.45.
parts.why: Small surprise fees are a classic hook.

parts.text: Pay within 12 hours
parts.why: A tight deadline is pressure to stop you thinking.

parts.text: or it will be returned to the sender.
royalmail-redelivery-uk.com
parts.why: Not an official Royal Mail address.

investigations.explanation: Check deliveries on the official website or app, never through a link in a text.

parts.text: Dear Customer,
parts.why: A generic greeting instead of your name.

parts.text: after our annual calculation you are owed a tax refund of £468.20.
Claim within 24 hours
parts.why: Urgency again.

parts.text: at hmrc-gov-refunds.net
parts.why: Official HMRC sites end in gov.uk.

parts.text: and enter your card details to receive it.
parts.why: Refunds never need your card details.

parts.text: Kind regards, HM Revenue & Customs.

investigations.explanation: HMRC doesn't send refund links. Forward scam emails to phishing@hmrc.gov.uk and texts to 7726.

parts.text: Hello, this is the fraud team at your bank.
We've spotted suspicious payments on your account.
To keep your money safe, move it to a new safe account now,
parts.why: Banks never ask you to move money to a safe account.

parts.text: don't tell anyone, not even staff in your branch,
parts.why: Asking for secrecy is a huge red flag.

parts.text: and read me the code we've just sent to your phone.
parts.why: One-time codes are for you only.

investigations.explanation: Hang up and call 159 or the number on your card, ideally from a different phone.

parts.text: I turned £250 into £8,000 in three weeks!
parts.why: Huge fast returns are the hook.

parts.text: Guaranteed profits, zero risk.
parts.why: No real investment is guaranteed.

parts.text: My account manager trades for you,
just send your deposit in crypto.
parts.why: Crypto payments are almost impossible to recover.

parts.text: Only 5 places left this week!
parts.why: Fake scarcity to rush you.

parts.text: Link in bio.

investigations.explanation: Check firms on the FCA Register and Warning List before investing.

parts.text: Work from home as a Payments Assistant.
Earn £500 a week, no experience needed.
parts.why: High pay for no experience is a warning sign.

parts.text: Receive payments into your own bank account and send them on to our partners,
parts.why: This is money muling, and it's illegal.

parts.text: keeping 10% for yourself.
parts.why: A cut for moving money is how mule recruiters tempt people.

parts.text: Flexible hours.

investigations.explanation: Never let anyone move money through your account.

parts.text: Brand new games console, still sealed.
£120 (normally £450).
parts.why: A price far below normal is the bait.

parts.text: Bank transfer only, no PayPal.
parts.why: Refusing protected payments removes your buyer protection.

parts.text: I'm working abroad, so a courier will deliver it.
parts.why: A seller you can't meet, plus a courier story.

parts.text: Happy to send more photos.

investigations.explanation: Use protected payments and see items in person when you can.

parts.text: MEGA CLEARANCE: 90% off all designer trainers!
parts.why: Unrealistic discounts on brands.

parts.text: Free UK delivery on orders over £50.
Pay by bank transfer for an extra 10% off.
parts.why: Pushing bank transfer means no card protection.

parts.text: Questions? Email shopdeals2026@gmail.com
parts.why: A real retailer uses its own email domain.

parts.text: Returns accepted within 14 days.

investigations.explanation: Check reviews and company details, and pay by card.

parts.text: Hi Mum, I dropped my phone in the bath.
This is my new number.
parts.why: A new number stops you checking with the real person.

parts.text: Can you pay a bill for me today? It's urgent.
parts.why: An urgent money request is the whole point.

parts.text: I can't talk on the phone right now,
parts.why: Avoiding a call stops you hearing it isn't them.

parts.text: love you x

investigations.explanation: Call them on their old number before sending anything.

parts.text: Ofgem: Energy Bill Rebate 2026.
You are entitled to a rebate of £315.
parts.why: Ofgem regulates energy. It doesn't email people rebates.

parts.text: To receive it, confirm your bank details
parts.why: Asking for bank details to “pay” you is a giveaway.

parts.text: before midnight tonight
parts.why: Artificial deadline.

parts.text: via ofgem-rebates-uk.com.
parts.why: Not an official gov.uk or ofgem.gov.uk address.

investigations.explanation: Any genuine energy support comes via your supplier or gov.uk, not a random email.

parts.text: Hi! I'm Sophie from a recruitment agency.
parts.why: Unsolicited job offers on WhatsApp are a common scam opener.

parts.text: We pay £100–£300 a day for liking videos online.
parts.why: Unrealistic pay for trivial tasks.

parts.text: You'll get small payments at first to build trust.
To unlock higher-paying tasks, just top up your account with a deposit.
parts.why: Paying to earn is the core of “task scams”.

parts.text: Reply YES to start.

investigations.explanation: Real employers never ask you to pay to work.

parts.text: Hi, I'd like to buy your sofa. I'll pay full price.
I've sent the money, check your email for the PayPal confirmation.
parts.why: Fake payment emails are used to rush you. Check the PayPal app itself.

parts.text: I accidentally sent £200 too much, please refund the extra by bank transfer.
parts.why: Overpayment refund requests are a classic trick.

parts.text: My courier will collect,
but you need to pay their £50 insurance fee first.
parts.why: Sellers never need to pay a buyer's courier.

investigations.explanation: Only trust payments you can see in your own account or app.

parts.text: ALERT: A new payee “J SMITH” was added to your account.
If this wasn't you,
call us urgently on 0800 046 1234.
parts.why: Never call a number given in an unexpected message. Use the one on your card.

parts.text: Your account will be frozen in 1 hour otherwise.
parts.why: Threats and deadlines are pressure tactics.

parts.text: Do not use your banking app as it may be compromised.
parts.why: Steering you away from your real app is a giveaway.

investigations.explanation: Check your banking app or call 159.

parts.text: PARKING CHARGE NOTICE.
You have parked in a restricted zone.
Pay £60 within 24 hours to avoid a £150 penalty.
parts.why: Extreme urgency is a pressure tactic.

parts.text: Scan the QR code to pay now.
parts.why: QR codes on unexpected notices can lead to fake payment sites.

parts.text: Payments accepted by bank transfer only.
parts.why: Legit operators offer proper payment options.

investigations.explanation: Check the operator independently and pay only through official channels.

parts.text: Your TV Licence Direct Debit has failed.
Your licence will be cancelled today
parts.why: Urgent cancellation threats are typical.

parts.text: unless you update your payment details
at tvlicensing-renewals.co.uk.
parts.why: Check the address carefully. Lookalike domains are common.

parts.text: Dear Valued Customer,
parts.why: Generic greeting.

investigations.explanation: Go to the official site by typing the address yourself.

parts.text: Lovely 2-bed flat in Zone 2, only £700 a month!
parts.why: Rent far below market rate.

parts.text: I'm the landlord but I'm working abroad,
parts.why: An owner who can't show you the property.

parts.text: so I can't show you around.
Send the deposit and first month's rent
parts.why: Paying before viewing is how renters lose money.

parts.text: and I'll post you the keys.

investigations.explanation: Never pay before viewing, and use a protected deposit scheme.

parts.text: Good morning, I'm calling about an exclusive opportunity.
parts.why: Unexpected calls about investments are a major red flag. Pension cold calling is illegal.

parts.text: Our clients earn 12% a year, guaranteed.
parts.why: Guaranteed returns don't exist.

parts.text: We're not on the FCA Register yet because we're so new,
parts.why: Unauthorised firms leave you without protection.

parts.text: but you need to decide today.
parts.why: Pressure to decide now.

parts.text: I'll send you a brochure.

investigations.explanation: Hang up, then check the firm on the FCA Register and Warning List.
